sections.overview: Eumorpha fasciatus, the banded sphinx, is a congener of E. anchemolus and E. labruscae, also covered in this set.
sections.identification: Its dark pinkish-brown wings carry pale bands and streaks, with pink patches on the hindwings; wingspan is about 8.7–9.6 cm.
sections.habitat: It ranges from northern Argentina through Central America and Mexico to the southern United States; far-northern records are strays.
sections.diet: Larvae feed mainly on primrose-willows and other evening primrose family plants; adults take flower nectar.
sections.behavior: Adults begin feeding at dusk, and several regional flight periods are recorded through much of the year.
sections.reproduction: Caterpillars pupate in shallow chambers or burrows in the soil; detailed egg-laying schedules are not summarized in the sources used.
sections.ecology: The three profiles are congeners, but their recorded larval hosts differ: this species uses the plant groups described above.
sections.conservation: BAMONA reports a globally secure category, while noting that the species may be rare near range edges.
